about: A recorded first-hour conversation, synthetic throughout (#2204). The owner gives one fresh small idea for their own selected repository (the one setup prepared), not the demo; the spec and its tickets come from this grill's answers, never a prepared plan. Steps name the install skill's onboarding road (WizSkills 0.3.0); tool steps run the installed onboarding helper against #1108's recording fakes.

options.label: as reported by CloudRoom; it may answer from a saved copy

turns.agent: OpenWiz is a factory of coding agents: they turn one thing you want into small tickets, build each one, review each other's work and merge it.

Your agents need a place to run: this machine, or Cloudroom or another cloud host to run many at once. Cloudroom uses your Cloud Credits. Each pull request is reviewed by the other model family, so a Codex fleet needs your Claude Code sign-in for its reviewer. Which would you like?

turns.user: In Cloudroom. My Claude Code sign-in is there for the reviewer.

turns.agent: Three ways to start: a small change in a repository you have, a fresh project from your idea, or something you have always wanted. Setup prepared synthetic-owner/synthetic-consumer; use that?

turns.user: My own repository, synthetic-owner/synthetic-consumer. I want a link checker for its docs.

turns.agent: Setup is next, for synthetic-owner/synthetic-consumer: your GitHub login is reused; create your own OpenWiz App (Create, then Install on this repository only) or skip it, prepare the project with your harness, model and effort, and make its private brain. Each effect is shown first.

turns.user: Create my App. Codex, syn-codex-model-01, high.

turns.agent: Q1: Check only relative links between the README and docs/ (recommended), or web links too? Q2: Print each broken link with its file and line (recommended), or only a count? Q3: Exit nonzero when any link is broken, so CI can use it (recommended)?

turns.user: Relative links only, file and line, and yes to the exit code.

turns.agent: Summary: a docs link checker for this repository: it finds Markdown links in README.md and docs/, checks each relative target exists, prints every broken link with its file and line, and exits nonzero when any is broken. If it matches what you want, say yes here.

spec.title: Spec: docs link checker
spec.body: Find Markdown links in README.md and docs/, check each relative target exists, print every broken link with its file and line, and exit nonzero when any is broken.

tickets.title: L3: print file and line for each broken link
L4: exit nonzero on a broken link
L5: document the checker in docs/

turns.agent: Ready: one fleet thread (codex, syn-codex-model-01, high) whose loop checks spec #920 every 10 minutes and starts 3 builders for L1, L2 and L3, each reviewed by claude-code from the other family. Start the fleet in Cloudroom now? It can cost money: it uses your Cloud Credits.
The plan passed its checks, so the fleet started: 3 builders, each on one small ticket. Watch them work at openwiz.dev/app; nothing for you to do until the first merge.
Three builders are working on L1 to L3; L4 and L5 wait for their blockers. Each pull request gets a claude-code review and CI, and merges once both pass on its exact head.
